x: We had great hopes however, of a placing with Stan Vickers, and Eric Hall, Kent and Surrey Champions, Syd James 2nd in the Surrey, George Checkley 5th in the Middlesex and Bob McMullen back from Canada and showing something like his old form, together with George Beecham, young Terry Clark and Ted Smith.
Bob Newson had now moved up and was fighting Dicky Green for another place, whilst Terry Clark and Hall of Surrey W.C. were also engaged in another private battle.
We eventually reached the venue quite safely and were there joined by Terry Clark who had travelled by rule of thumb, and were ready to take on all comers.
Arriving at the changing room we were met by Terry Clark looking spick and span in his R.A.F uniform. He's got so many stripes on his arm that we nicknamed him "The walking Zebra".

Youngsters, and new scoring members of our County team were Nick Milsum and Terry Clark who finished 8th and 10th respectively. Both grand efforts and Ben Clark, an old Belgravian, must have been proud to see his son winning his first County Medal.
Our younger members are showing that they are not to be outdone by setting a new Surrey County record in the one mile Walk, Terry Clark taking first place in 7m. 14s and Nick Milsum 2nd in 7m. 21s.

Terry Clark won this trophy in the very good time of 40m.04s. with Trevor Luck 2nd in 41.07 and Nick Milsum 3rd in 41.24. Although it is difficult to get a big field for this race as it coincides with the age for National Service, I hope there will be a few more next year.
The Junior Walk Record had stood to Jack Rutland for exactly 20 years until Terry Clark won the Surrey Junior Championship in the time given above.

At the same meeting we had two entries in the Junior one mile walk with Terry Clark and Nick Milsum. They both walked exceptionally well with good, fair walking and were a credit to our Walking Section.

Ray Middleton, home from Ireland, walked well to finish 6th in 41m.21s., Dave Stevens (individual) was 7th, Nick Milsum 9th and Terry Clark, who walked a blinder on the last lap, was 12th and Trevor Luck 13th.
Unfortunately we lost both Terry Clark and John Knifton who came under the judge's ban when in 2nd and 4th positions thus ruining any chances of winning the team race.
Terry Clark was always handy and he was followed by Joe Coleman who took first veteran's prize. Nick Milsum was third in the handicap and of course we won the team award - a very successful pot hunt.

We lost Nick Milsum and Terry Clark of our first team men, but their turn will come. Nick was particularly unfortunate for he was our fourth man, on the last lap and, in the view of many, walking splendidly as he came through the field.

…oufleges no ordinary resoluteness, the strength of Ray Middleton who must be a future champion, the potential powers of Terry Clark and Brian Cornick, and so through the team to our last man, Percy Wilson, who so typifies the fun and enjoyment obtained from the sport.…

The course consisted of one small lap and a larger one of fairly good roads with not too much traffic. Terry Clark headed the field from the start and was never overtaken. The good walking of a "dark horse" in the person of Flt.Lt.
He was ably supported by George Williams 2nd, Ray Hall 6th and Terry Clark(still a junior) 8th. The fine walking of John Knifton in his first 10 mile race was encouraging.
Terry Clark gave a creditable display in his first Senior R.W.A. championship. It is unfortunate that the times are suspect owing to a misunderstanding at the turning point.

Eric Hall went into the lead immediately, accompanied by Terry Clark who only completed two laps of the course. Halfway times were not outstanding; Eric and Terry Clark were still leading with Ray Hall in 3rd place closely followed by Cyril Yescombe and George Beecham who were about three minutes in…

Credit must also be accorded to Terry Clark, only just out of the junior stage, for his very fine effort in finishing ninth. Although we lost the team race we did retain the Nijmegen Cup for the first club to finish eight men, indeed this is the fifth time in succession that we have won it.

We are pleased to learn that George Checkley is recovering from his illness, and hopes to start training again. Congratulations to Terry Clark on his recent wedding to Janet. Several Club members attended the ceremony.

Our good wishes also go to Eric Gebbett on his marriage, and Terry Clark who has also taken a wife unto himself. We hope to welcome Jack Brown back from Cyprus in Mar/April of next year, and it will be pleasing indeed to see him in our teams once again.
Congratulations also to Ray Hall on his engagement and best wishes to Terry Clark who sends his regards from South Australia where he is on R.A.F. duty.
This year we were without the services of Terry Clark at present in Australia, and we knew the holders, Metropolitan W.C. would pay us the compliment of fighting every inch of the way.
A few days on the road, amid outstanding scenery, found us in Adelaide where we stayed with Terry Clark - Belgrave's national junior champion in 1958.
